findings.summary: Fibery reached public release on April 1, 2020.
Fibery is a connected, configurable workspace for teams that need linked operational and knowledge data.
Users repeatedly value the relational database model, workflow flexibility, connected information, and ability to replace several narrower tools.
Customer support and the pace of product improvement receive repeated positive mentions.
The flexibility carries a real setup cost and learning curve. Teams must design their system before the product delivers its full value.
Reporting, dashboards, external sharing, permissions clarity, notifications, and specialized resource planning appear as narrower but concrete weak spots.
No new hands-on test was performed. Current claims must not repeat old complaints, such as the historical absence of mobile apps, without fresh verification.

sources.excerpt: Users praise flexibility and customization, while many note a steep learning curve.
sources.summary: G2 showed 125 reviews. Recurring strengths were linked data, adaptable workflows, databases, whiteboards, and support. Setup effort and the learning curve were the clearest repeated drawbacks.
sources.title: Fibery Reviews 2026

sources.excerpt: Verified reviewers praise connected databases and support, while reporting setup, sharing, dashboards, and planning limits.
sources.summary: Capterra showed 52 reviews with 4.2 ease of use and 4.9 customer service. Reviews support the flexibility theme but add concrete weaknesses in reporting, external sharing, visual features, and resource planning.
sources.title: Fibery Reviews 2026

sources.excerpt: Reviewers describe a flexible workspace shaped around real processes.
sources.summary: Product Hunt showed 37 reviews. The recurring use cases span product work, research, CRM, operations, documentation, and portfolio management, with praise for linked data and responsive support.
sources.title: Fibery Reviews

sources.excerpt: Users call Fibery powerful after the setup curve, while pointing to notifications and the then-missing mobile app as gaps.
sources.summary: The thread validates the core tradeoff: unusual flexibility and an engaged team, offset by setup complexity and feature gaps. Dated complaints must not be repeated as current facts.
sources.title: Pros and Cons of Fibery?

sources.excerpt: Verified customers praise flexibility and support, but cite dashboard, permissions, stability, and planning limits.
